etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Late Latin vacantia. Doublet of vacance.

quote.citation: 1965, Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution:
quote.text: Whenever there is a vacancy in the office of the Vice President, the President shall nominate a Vice President who shall take office upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress.

definitions.definition: An available room in a hotel; guest house, etc.

quote.citation: 1993, James Michie, trans. Ovid, The Art of Love, Book II:
quote.text: Sky was set above earth, land ringed with sea, / Chaos retired to its own vacancy [...].

definitions.definition: A blank mind, unoccupied with thought.

quote.citation: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter I, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume III, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 2:
quote.text: ...—who has not looked back to the past with that passion of hopelessness, which deems that life can never more be what it has been,—with a consciousness that the dearer emotions are exhausted, while in their place have arisen but vacancy and weariness?

definitions.definition: (physics) A defect in a crystal caused by the absence of an atom in a lattice
